clue.text: Skill? No, disaster, sadly

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters of the preceding words are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: Someone insists the botched job showed no skill at all: it was simply a disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges the ten letters of NO DISASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: deftness or dexterity is a kind of skill.

clue.text: Marked rise in river — a lot of risk about that

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the second
a lot of, but not all, means the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: to risk is to dice, as in dicing with death

indicators.note: in a down clue a rise means the river's name is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the Tamar is the river dividing Devon from Cornwall

explanation.surface: A report on a river level jumping sharply, with flooding a real risk.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rise' turns the river upwards; the Tamar divides Devon from Cornwall. 'that' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a marked change is a striking, dramatic one.

clue.text: No strong material to go to court after position upheld

indicators.note: after places the court action following the position piece
upheld in a down clue means the word is lifted to read bottom to top

parts.note: to sit is to take up a position, as a model does
to sue is to take someone to court

explanation.surface: A legal flavour: a weak case fails once someone's position is upheld in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upheld' reads the position word bottom to top, as suits a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: tissue paper or fabric is thin and flimsy, hardly a strong material.

clue.text: Waste large satellite's power during repair

indicators.note: during places the satellite and power letters within the repair word

parts.note: to mend is to repair
the ISS, International Space Station, is a large artificial satellite
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A complaint about funds squandered while a big satellite's power supply is being fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to squander money or effort is to waste it.

clue.text: Moving round borders of state etc, not given to stays

indicators.note: moving these letters around rearranges them into a new order
the borders of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone moving around a state's borders and so on, never one to stay put anywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stays' are the stiffening strips of a corset, not visits; 'Moving' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Stays are corset stiffeners, so one not given to wearing them goes without that garment.

clue.text: Old soldier about to stop cheers for feud

indicators.note: the soldier wraps about the stopping word

parts.note: a vet is a veteran, an old soldier
to end is to stop
ta is British informal thanks, like cheers

explanation.surface: A veteran trying to put a stop to the drinking toasts that fuel an old feud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheers' here is thanks, not a toast: both are casual British ways of saying thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a vendetta is a prolonged bitter feud, often between families.

clue.text: Volume is ready for penning one dream

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
on can mean ready to go, as in a show being on

explanation.surface: An author's book is ready for writing up one dream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' looks like writing but means enclosing, as sheep in a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a vision can be something seen in a dream or reverie.

clue.text: Pro runs, restricted by recent wound

indicators.note: restricted by means held within the recent word

parts.note: late can mean recent, as in the late news
an ace is an expert, a pro
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A professional cricketer's run-scoring is held back by a fresh injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restricted by' puts ACER inside LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to lacerate is to tear the flesh, wounding it.

clue.text: Dutch heretic securing victory regarding evolution

indicators.note: securing means holding, so the heretic holds the victory

parts.note: an Arian followed Arius, whose views on the Trinity were declared heresy
a win is a victory

explanation.surface: A Dutch dissenter claims a win in the debate about evolution.
explanation.walkthrough: Arius was a fourth-century priest whose teaching on Christ's divinity was condemned as heresy.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive: Charles Darwin's theory of natural selection made his name the adjective for evolutionary ideas.

clue.text: Energy of life not entirely evident in South American figure

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: not entirely shown, so the last letter goes missing

parts.note: vital means of or relating to life

explanation.surface: A sense that the energy of life is hard to see in some South American figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely evident' drops the last letter from VITAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Name: Eva Perón, Argentina's first lady, is known by the diminutive that titles the musical.

clue.text: Diffusion very much set back one probing simple plant life

indicators.note: set back means the two letters are turned round

parts.note: so means very much, as in so tired

indicators.note: probing means poking into, so the one goes inside the plant

parts.note: moss is a simple non-flowering plant
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A botanist's note: spreading is badly delayed as someone investigates primitive plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set back' turns the two-letter intensifier round; 'probing' sends the one into the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Technical synonym: the passage of fluid through a membrane is a form of diffusion.

clue.text: Historic dome, lit spookily

indicators.note: spookily suggests eerie shifting, so the letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: An ancient domed building, eerily lit at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spookily' rearranges DOMELIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something from the past, old-fashioned or belonging to former days, is historic.

clue.text: Basis to claim small amount half-heartedly

indicators.note: half the heart, the double letter at the centre, is removed

parts.note: a tittle is a tiny amount, as in jot or tittle

explanation.surface: Someone making a claim for a small sum without much conviction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' removes one of the two middle Ts of TITTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal sense: a title is a right or entitlement, the ground on which ownership is claimed.

clue.text: Reference to history: quite a few involved in rout

indicators.note: involved in means set inside the rout word

parts.note: to paste is informal for to thrash or rout
tens, as in tens of people, means quite a few

explanation.surface: A historical note that many soldiers took part in the rout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rout' is the verb to thrash, for which paste is informal British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar: verbs in this tense refer to past events, a playful reading of history.

clue.text: Classify version of gene pool, including one with separate source of heredity

indicators.note: a version is a reworking, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A geneticist sorting a variant gene pool, including a distinct origin of inheritance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version of' rearranges GENEPOOL with I and H (the 'source of' HEREDITY) added in; 'including' and 'with separate' bring those two letters into the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb sense: to put something in a category, as letters go in compartments, is to classify it.

clue.text: Clear tour's abandoned part of London

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters run riot

explanation.surface: A sightseeing tour is called off in a district of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' rearranges CLEARTOURS. EARLS COURT is a district of west London, once home to a big exhibition centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Place: this west London district is one area of the capital.

clue.text: Times vary in the endless career developed for travelling educator

indicators.note: the times-vary piece sits in the anagram
developed means worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged
endless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as times
to change is to vary

explanation.surface: Schedules shift in an educator's career as it develops through travel abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims the last letter of career; 'developed' rearranges it with 'the' into ETEACHER, and the times-vary piece sits 'in' after its first E.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a teacher swapping posts with a colleague abroad for a term travels to teach.

clue.text: A quantity of sewage, though no initial flush

indicators.note: no initial means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: effluent is liquid waste or sewage

explanation.surface: A volume of waste water that, oddly, no first flush shifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flush' looks like the toilet but means rich. 'no initial' drops the E of EFFLUENT, and A goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: someone flush with cash is wealthy.

clue.text: Smell — it will be found in some people

parts.note: hum is British slang for a bad smell

indicators.note: will be found in means placed inside the next word

parts.note: any can mean some, as in have you any?

explanation.surface: An observation that a body odour turns up in certain individuals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smell' as hum is British slang for a nasty odour; 'some people' splits, with 'people' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Collective noun: the human race as a whole is people in general.

clue.text: Betrayed and beaten up for documents but showing composure

parts.note: to sing or sang is slang for informing on accomplices, betraying them

indicators.note: beaten up means knocked about, so the three letters are jumbled

parts.note: ID means identity documents

explanation.surface: An informer, roughed up for his papers, nevertheless keeps his cool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Betrayed' as sang is underworld slang for informing; 'beaten up' jumbles 'for' into FRO.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: coolness under pressure, literally cold blood in French, is composure.

clue.text: Latest song on the radio? There's no coverage here

indicators.note: on the radio means heard rather than seen, so the words are judged by how they are spoken

parts.note: latest is new and a song is a ditty

explanation.surface: A radio presenter plays the newest track, but nobody is reporting on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coverage' looks like press reporting but means clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: being naked means having nothing covering the body.

clue.text: French writer caught with two Americans?

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
AM for American and US for the United States are two ways of saying American

explanation.surface: A French author is caught in the company of a pair of Americans.
explanation.definitionFit: Name: Albert Camus wrote The Outsider and The Plague in French.

clue.text: Fighting? Doctor having one put in bed

indicators.note: put in means placed inside the bed word

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
a means one

explanation.surface: A doctor admits a patient to a bed, then asks whether there was a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is the British basic medical degree, so it stands for a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: combat is armed fighting between forces.

clue.text: Mercy given to Communist in Cornish town

parts.note: red is a common label for a Communist
ruth is an old word for pity or mercy, the opposite of ruthless

explanation.surface: Mercy shown to a Communist in a town in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: RUTH survives mainly in ruthless. REDRUTH is a town in Cornwall, the county at England's south-west tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Place: this former mining town lies in western Cornwall.

clue.text: See 8
Pepper pot cracked, one lot of pieces falling inside

indicators.note: falling inside means dropping into the broken pot
cracked means broken, so the letters of pot are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
chessmen are pieces, so a lot of them are men

explanation.surface: A kitchen accident: a pepper pot cracks and bits drop into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracked' rearranges 'pot' into PTO; chess pieces are often called men.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the pimento is a mild red pepper, often stuffed into olives.

clue.text: See 4
Major figure's beat including computer work

indicators.note: including means the beat word goes around the computer piece

parts.note: to tan is to thrash or beat
IT is information technology, computer work

explanation.surface: An important figure's routine round now includes some computing tasks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat' looks like a patrol route but means thrash. 'including' puts IT in TAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Metaphor: a giant in their field, after the mythical Greek giants, is a major figure.

clue.text: Historic house with new actors in revolutionary material

indicators.note: the new actors go in the reversed word
revolutionary means turned round, so the four letters read backwards

parts.note: material in the sense of real and substantial
the actors in a play make up its cast

explanation.surface: A stately home brings in new actors to perform some revolutionary material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' looks like cloth but means real; 'revolutionary' makes LAER. Lancaster was a royal house in the Wars of the Roses.
explanation.definitionFit: History: the royal dynasty of Henry IV, V and VI is a historic house.
